title: Headrest
attribution: Fijian; the catalogue does not name its maker
observation: The catalogue places this wood-and-fibre headrest at Bau and gives its length as 64.5 cm. It marks the approximate date with a question.
name: Headrest from Bau
stake: The cutter has drawn a two-column timeline. One column is for dated records. The other can hold an estimate with its question mark.
detail: The Met gives a length of 64.5 cm and dates this headrest to about 1862, with a question mark.
bellDetail: Sora leaves a margin for the estimate on the dock timeline. A traveller asks where the question mark came from.
bellSource: Sora clips a finder to the Bau record. She leaves its place on the timeline open until the dated line arrives.
trace: Renna files an estimate card with a question mark the same size as the date. The reader who left before the bell can find it by the record number.
altText: A long wooden rest with a shallow curve and two legs, photographed from the side.

title: Tapa Cloth
attribution: Fiji Islands maker unidentified in the catalogue
observation: This accession has a recorded length of 381 cm and width of 73.1 cm. Its exact production year stays open.
name: Tapa cloth from Fiji
stake: Two guides for tapa cloth have the same heading. A carrier needs to keep the measured strip with the cloth it describes.
detail: This cloth measures 381 by 73.1 cm. The catalogue places its making before 1971.
bellDetail: Sora sets a long strip on the working guide. She keeps its end free until the clerk confirms which record it belongs to.
bellSource: Sora sets the number beside the guide’s title. It keeps the two cloths apart while the strip is still on the line.
trace: Renna attaches the long strip and its width line to this accession. A reader can use the guide to compare the two records without swapping measurements.
altText: A long rectangular bark cloth with repeating dark and light motifs and a banded border.

title: Tapa Cloth
medium: Probably mulberry bark (Broussonetia papyrifera), two pieces joined together
attribution: Hawaiian maker unidentified in the catalogue
observation: The catalogue describes two joined pieces and gives an overall measurement of 31.2 × 20.7 cm. The identification of the plant material is tentative.
name: Joined tapa cloth from Hawaiʻi
stake: The crew copied the words “two pieces” down twice. The next reader needs to see whether the dimensions describe the join or each piece.
detail: The catalogue measures the two joined pieces together at 31.2 by 20.7 cm. It gives the material as probably mulberry bark.
bellDetail: Sora closes a plain clasp over both practice scraps. She puts the combined measurement outside the clasp. Its record line still needs to arrive.
bellSource: Sora leaves space beneath this exact number for an assembly line. The copy can wait there without assigning an extra measurement to each piece.
trace: Renna files the join and measurement together. The word “probably” stays by the plant material when the copy is drawn again.
altText: A joined cloth with dark diamond-like marks on one piece and rusty red patterned bands on the other.

title: Woman's Sash
medium: Dyed plantfiber; plain weave, twill weave and floats
attribution: Woman’s sash associated with the Caroline Islands; maker unidentified in the catalogue
observation: The museum identifies dyed plant fibre, plain weave, twill and floats on a sash whose measured extent is 172.7 × 10.2 cm. Its date is tentative.
name: Sash attributed to the Caroline Islands
stake: A visitor’s rough sketch shows a long band. The receiving table needs a fibre and technique line for this object.
detail: The catalogue lists dyed plant fibre and three features of the cloth: plain weave, twill weave and floats. It dates it tentatively to around the 1900s.
bellDetail: Sora puts three spaces on the working line for the cloth features. She leaves the caption unsigned while she waits for the numbered source.
bellSource: Sora files a source for this sash without deciding what the visitor’s rough lines show. The technique line can be checked from that record.
trace: Renna copies all three terms beside the numbered sash record. The visitor can ask for a close view of one technique at a time.
altText: A long narrow band with changes of colour and pattern along the length.

title: Bowl
attribution: Mā’ohi artist, unnamed in the catalogue; Austral Islanders
observation: The record lists wood and distinguishes the bowl’s 16.8 cm width from its 30.8 cm depth.
name: Wooden bowl from the Austral Islands
stake: The front and end views of a bowl are loose in the reader’s tray. The carrier needs the width and depth to stay on their own edges.
detail: The Met lists a 16.8 cm width and a 30.8 cm depth for this bowl by an unnamed Mā’ohi artist.
bellDetail: Sora turns the loose guide so its depth runs along the longer edge. She holds off naming the record until the source clasp arrives.
bellSource: Sora puts the exact accession on both views. The clerk can keep them together while the edge dimensions come across.
trace: Renna gives the width and depth their own arrows on the full guide. The carving and maker’s name remain separate questions.
altText: A dark wooden bowl in side view, with a long rim and raised ends.

title: Tahiì (fan)
attribution: Ènata artist, unnamed in the catalogue; Marquesan (Enata) people
observation: The catalogue identifies wood, whalebone and fibre in an Ènata fan and records its thickness separately from its height and width.
name: Tahiì by an Ènata artist
stake: A flat sketch has room for the front view alone. A reader has asked whether the thin edge and the named materials are part of the same accession.
detail: This tahiì measures 47 by 43.2 cm with a depth of 2.5 cm. The Met lists wood, whalebone and fibre.
bellDetail: Sora leaves an edge line with the depth on the working sketch. She has room for all three materials when the source catch arrives.
bellSource: Sora keeps the Tahiì number with the sketch. The clerk can already find the exact fan while its edge and materials wait at the latch.
trace: Renna attaches a separate edge view to the exact record and leaves the source’s three named materials together.
altText: A broad, rounded woven fan with a short, narrow handle.

title: Cast of a Pot Sherd
date: Cast made in the mid-20th century
attribution: Cast maker unrecorded; catalogue associates the represented form with Lapita people
place: Santa Cruz Islands, Temotu Province, Solomon Islands, the place given for the represented form
observation: The accession is a 7.3 cm-high plaster cast of a pot sherd. The museum’s date applies to the cast.
name: Plaster cast of a pot sherd
stake: Someone put a date on the representation. The draft still has a blank where it should say which object the date is about.
detail: This is a 7.3 cm-high plaster cast made in the mid-20th century. The date describes the cast of the sherd.
bellDetail: Sora moves the date onto a cast slip. She leaves the represented form’s date line open while the number is coming across.
bellSource: Sora attaches the sherd cast’s accession to the teaching slip. The date line stays open until the detail arrives.
trace: Renna copies “date of the cast” onto this accession’s own line. The slip gives the represented sherd its own empty date space.
altText: An irregular grey plaster cast with repeated markings across its visible face.

title: Cast of a Dish
date: Cast made in the mid-20th century
attribution: Cast maker unrecorded; catalogue associates the represented form with Lapita people
place: Santa Cruz Islands, Temotu Province, Solomon Islands, the place given for the represented form
observation: This is a separately accessioned plaster cast of a dish. Its 17.5 cm recorded height is a dimension of the cast.
name: Plaster cast of a dish
stake: The register already has a sherd cast next to this dish cast. The two bare slips can be mixed up if a visitor searches by period alone.
detail: The Met records this dish cast separately, at 17.5 cm high, and dates the making of the plaster cast to the mid-20th century.
bellDetail: Sora makes a 17.5 cm guide for the working tray. She leaves the number blank until she can confirm which of the two casts it describes.
bellSource: Sora opens an individual line for the dish cast. The two casts can keep separate shelf locations while the clerk waits for the full description.
trace: Renna links the two separately accessioned casts in the ledger. A reader can retrieve the dish by number without treating the cast date as the date of its model.
altText: A plaster cast of a shallow dish, showing a curved rim and patches of differing grey tones.
